index.intro: Hesoyam. Colors, type, materials, and components live in {ui}.
index.colorsBody: High-contrast scales on dark-first tokens. Ten steps per hue, plus gray-alpha and two backgrounds.
index.iconsBody: Lucide through the shared Icon wrapper.
index.blocksBody: Hairline table for page chrome. Title, tiles, and sections share one rule — no stacked cards.
index.label: Label
index.materialsBody: Radius, hairline borders, and elevation. 6px controls, 8px cards, 12px menus. Docs chrome stays square.
index.importDescription: Named exports from {pkg}. Setup lives on {installation}.
index.rulesBlocks: Docs chrome follows {blocks}: full-width hairlines, not a column of rounded cards.
index.rulesBorders: Hairline borders use {border}. Primary text is {primary}, secondary is {secondary}.
index.rulesAliases: shadcn aliases stay so older screens compile: Button {ghost} → tertiary, {outline} → secondary.
index.rulesLeftovers: Card and Sidebar have no Hesoyam analog. Leave those folders; they are leftovers, not replacements.

avatar.title: Avatar
avatar.description: Face or initials for a person, team, or org. Stack two or more with AvatarGroup.
avatar.groupHint: Pass members and a pixel size. limit shows a +N count for the rest.
avatar.stackingOrderHint: First member sits on top. reverse puts the last member on top. Left-to-right order stays the same.
avatar.overlapHint: overlap auto scales with size. A number is pixels of overlap — higher packs tighter.
avatar.sizeHint: Pixel size is the Hesoyam API. Token aliases sm (24), default (32), and lg (48) still work.
avatar.gitHint: GitHubAvatar, GitLabAvatar, and BitbucketAvatar resolve the host avatar from username.
avatar.withCustomIconHint: Overlay a status glyph. Use the icon slot; keep icon-background when the mark needs a disc.
avatar.letterHint: 1–2 uppercase initials when there is no photo. This port renders letter only when placeholder is off.
avatar.placeholderHint: Loading shell. Not a permanent fallback — switch to src, username, or letter once you know the entity.
avatar.badgeHint: AvatarBadge sits on the corner. Empty it is a presence dot; slot an icon at 32px and up.
avatar.imageAndFallbackHint: Compound slots when you already have a URL and do not want the username resolver.
avatar.bestPractice1: One person, team, or org is {avatar}. Two or more stacked faces is {avatarGroup} so overlap, size, and the overflow count stay consistent.
avatar.bestPractice2: Resolve a photo with {src} or {username} first. Fall back to {letter} (1–2 uppercase chars). Keep {placeholder} for the loading shell.
avatar.bestPractice3: {title} is the entity name. Letter avatars already announce Avatar with initials — do not prefix "Avatar of".
avatar.bestPractice4: Match adjacent type: 20–24px next to 13px meta, 32px next to 14px body, 48px and up in headers.
avatar.bestPractice5: Status lives on {avatarWithIcon} or {avatarBadge}, not a second overlapping Avatar.

badge.title: Badge
badge.description: Short label for status, plan, environment, or role. Sits next to the thing it describes.
badge.variantsHint: Color plus contrast. high is the solid fill. low is the subtle chip for dense rows.
badge.sizesHint: Hesoyam sizes are sm, md, and lg. small and large are aliases for sm and lg.
badge.withIconsHint: One icon via the icon slot, then the label. Do not stack two icons.
badge.pillHint: Link-shaped chip. Less loud than a Button. Render as an anchor with {as} set to {a}.
badge.bestPractice1: Badge is static metadata. One per row. A clickable filter is {pill} or a small Button — do not hang a click handler on a status chip.
badge.bestPractice2: Map meaning to color: {green} healthy, {red} error, {amber} warning, {blue} informational, {gray} neutral. Low contrast tones any of them down.
badge.bestPractice3: Title Case, one word when you can, two max: {active}, {pending}, {enterpriseTrial}. The row supplies the sentence.
badge.bestPractice4: Skip a check icon for success or an X for errors — the variant already carries that. Pair Alpha / Beta with a Tooltip that names the limit.
badge.bestPractice5: Set {title} when the badge is icon-only or ambiguous. Do not rely on color alone.
badge.bestPractice6: Aliases {default}, {secondary}, {destructive}, {outline}, {ghost}, and {link} remain for older screens. New code should use Hesoyam color names.

banner.title: Banner
banner.description: Full-width status strip for a single announcement. Optional action via the button prop.
banner.defaultHint: Message in the default slot. button takes href, content, and an optional onClick.
banner.withoutActionHint: Omit button when there is nothing to do except read.
banner.previewPlainMessage: Scheduled maintenance starts Friday at 18:00 UTC.
banner.bestPractice1: Banner spans its container. Use it for a page- or layout-level announcement, not a field error and not a Toast.
banner.bestPractice2: One banner at a time. A second strip means the first message was not resolved.
banner.bestPractice3: Keep the copy to one sentence. Lead with the fact, then the window or impact. The action label is a verb:
banner.bestPractice4b: when the control changes the URL. Use
banner.bestPractice5: This port has no variant or dismiss prop. Persistent product chrome belongs in the layout; a closable notice is a Note or Toast.

blocks.title: Blocks
blocks.description: Page chrome is a table, not a stack of cards. Full-width hairlines divide title, tiles, and sections. Radius stays on controls.
blocks.hairlineTableDesc: {gap} on a {token} fill. Cells paint the page color back on.
blocks.titleBandDesc: {component} is the first row. The stripe under the description is the top of the next block.
blocks.anatomyDesc: Every Hesoyam docs page is the same three rows. Components add previews inside a section; they do not start a second layout.
blocks.anatomy01Desc: 40px title, 16px secondary, padding in the cell, hairline under the whole band.
blocks.anatomy02Desc: Optional 2- or 3-column tiles. Shared rules, no gap, no radius. Use {href} when the cell is a link.
blocks.anatomy03Desc: 24px heading plus body. Another full-width rule under the band. Live demos sit inside, not beside.
blocks.anatomy04Desc: Inset frame at card radius (8px). The only rounded box on a docs page. Code is the next row of that frame.
blocks.usageCallout: Keep {class} on the page root so older pages compile. The layout sets it to zero — spacing is the hairline, not a gap.
blocks.doItem1: Stack page chrome as full-width bands: title, then cells, then sections. One shared hairline between each.
blocks.doItem2: Use --ds-gray-alpha-400 for every rule. Same token on header, sidebar, cells, and preview frames.
blocks.doItem3: Put DocsCells next to DocsPageHeader when the tiles are the page, not inside a padded section.
blocks.doItem4: Keep radius 0 on the page table. Round only the control or the preview frame inside a cell.
blocks.dontItem1: Do not wrap a page in gap + rounded cards. That breaks the table and doubles the borders.
blocks.dontItem2: Do not invent a second hairline color or a 2px rule for “emphasis”.
blocks.dontItem3: Do not add space-y between DocsPageHeader, DocsCells, and DocsSection — the layout zeroes it.
blocks.dontItem4: Do not put page padding on {main}. Padding lives on the cell, so rules can run edge to edge.

breadcrumbs.title: Breadcrumbs
breadcrumbs.description: Path from a section root to the current page. type text is the trail. type menu opens siblings.
breadcrumbs.defaultDescription: text is a slash-separated trail. menu paints each crumb as a compact control.
breadcrumbs.activeDescription: Mark the current page with active. That item gets aria-current page.
breadcrumbs.disabledDescription: A segment that belongs in the path but is not reachable.
breadcrumbs.menuSlotDescription: On type menu, the menu slot fills Menu. Use MenuItem for each sibling.
breadcrumbs.bestPractice1: Breadcrumbs orient, they do not replace primary nav. Three to five levels is enough; collapse the middle if the path is longer.
breadcrumbs.bestPractice2Before: The last crumb is the current page and gets
breadcrumbs.bestPractice3Menu: only when a crumb has siblings the user might jump to.
breadcrumbs.bestPractice4Before: Disable a segment that exists in the hierarchy but has no page. Do not leave a dead
breadcrumbs.bestPractice5Before: Labels are Title Case nouns that match the page title:

button.title: Button
button.description: Trigger an action. Use ButtonLink when the control changes the URL.
button.sizesHint: Default in this port is small (32px), matching product chrome. medium is 40px, large is 48px.
button.shapesHint: Icon-only buttons need svg-only and an aria-label.
button.customHint: Override foreground, background, and border for normal / hover / active.
button.bpStateVsLink: Button mutates state. ButtonLink changes the URL. More than one related action in a row → Menu or Split Button.
button.bpVariants: Primary is {primary}. Supporting is {supporting}. Destructive confirmations use {destructive}.
button.bpFormSubmit: Form submit uses {submit}. Visual variant stays on {variant} / {type}.
button.bpLoading: Pass {loading} instead of swapping a spinner so the control stays focusable.
button.bpDisabled: Disable only when the action is impossible. Explain why with a Tooltip.
button.bpAliases: Aliases {ghost} → tertiary and {outline} → secondary exist for older screens. New code should use Hesoyam names.

calendar.title: Calendar
calendar.description: Range picker with a trigger, month grid, optional presets, and time fields. Click the trigger to open.
calendar.defaultHint: value plus {'@change'}. allow-clear shows an × when a range is set. min-value and max-value clamp the grid.
calendar.horizontalLayoutHint: horizontal-layout puts presets beside the grid. Hide times with show-time-input false.
calendar.sizesHint: medium is the default trigger (32px). small is 28px and tightens the grid.
calendar.presetsHint: Record of CalendarPreset. Each entry needs text, start, and end.
calendar.compactHint: Tighter padding. Presets wrap in a row above the grid.
calendar.stackedHint: Presets above the month. Use this in a sidebar or any narrow column.
calendar.presetDefaultHint: preset-index selects a preset on mount when value is empty. Index is the key order.
calendar.minMaxDatesHint: Days outside the window are disabled. Bind the data retention range, not an arbitrary year.
calendar.pinnedTimezoneHint: pinned-timezone locks the zone and renders it as read-only text instead of a select.
calendar.bestPractice1: Calendar is a range picker for analytics windows and any surface where weekday and month context matter. A single typed ISO date is an Input.
calendar.bestPractice2: Ship presets for the common windows ({preset7}, {presetMonth}). {stacked} in a sidebar; {horizontal} when results sit beside the popover.
calendar.bestPractice3: Set {minValue} and {maxValue} to the data you actually have. Do not let people pick outside retention.
calendar.bestPractice4: Keep {value} after the popover closes so the next open can tweak the end date. {vModel} is the Vue alias for {value} + {change}.
calendar.bestPractice5: Default the timezone to the viewer. Use {pinned} only when the report is locked to a region. Do not silently render UTC for a Pacific viewer.
calendar.bestPractice6: The trigger already labels the committed range. Do not replace it with “Pick a date” after a value is set.

card.title: Card
card.description: Leftover shadcn surface. Hesoyam has no Card analog — keep this folder, do not invent a replacement.
card.defaultHint: Compound parts: Card, CardHeader, CardTitle, CardDescription, CardAction, CardContent, CardFooter. size is default or sm.
card.callout: Card is leftover shadcn. New product UI should not grow a parallel “Hesoyam card”. For a hover preview with identity and a few facts, use Context Card. For a settings block with a title and footer actions, use Fieldset.
card.practiceNoPort: Do not port Hesoyam “cards” here. Existing screens that already import Card can stay.
card.practiceFieldset: New settings copy belongs in Fieldset. Hover identity belongs in Context Card.
card.practiceSizeAfter: tightens padding and gap. Do not invent a third size.
card.practiceCardAction: Put the trailing control in CardAction so the header grid keeps title and description on the left.
card.practiceTokensBefore: Tokens only. Hairline on footer uses

checkbox.title: Checkbox
checkbox.description: Toggle a single option on or off. Use a group when the user can pick more than one.
checkbox.defaultHint: Hesoyam API is checked plus {'@change'}. v-model and v-model:checked are Vue aliases.
checkbox.indeterminateHint: Visual only. Drive it from a parent that knows a subset is selected. It is not a third model value.
checkbox.practiceMultiSelect: Multi-select in a list, table rows, or an opt-in group. A single boolean setting (dark mode, password protection) is a Switch.
checkbox.practiceIndeterminateBefore: Indeterminate is a dash, not a stored third state. Clear it as soon as every child is fully checked or unchecked. Name the partial count in the group label when it helps:
checkbox.practiceRequiredAck: Required acknowledgments validate on submit, not on blur. Checking and unchecking should not flash an error.
checkbox.practiceDisable: Disable only when the choice is impossible, and say why with a Tooltip. A grey box with no reason reads as a bug.
checkbox.practiceLabelBefore: The label is the click target. A row-select box with no visible text needs
checkbox.practiceGroupLabelBefore: Group label is a Title Case noun:
checkbox.practiceGroupLabelAfter: An acknowledgment is a full sentence with a period:
checkbox.practiceAckExample: I agree to the Terms of Service.

code-block.title: Code Block
code-block.description: Syntax-highlighted source the reader will scan or paste. Pair with Snippet for a one-line command.
code-block.defaultHint: Pass filename and language so the header and highlighter have something to work with.
code-block.noFilenameHint: Omit the header when the snippet is ephemeral. Copy sits on the block instead.
code-block.highlightedLinesHint: Mark only the lines under discussion. Highlighting every line is the same as highlighting none.
code-block.addedAndRemovedHint: Use addedLinesNumbers and removedLinesNumbers. Do not fake a diff with comments — those copy with the snippet.
code-block.referencedLinesHint: Click a line number to pin that row and write {'#L{n}'} into the URL.
code-block.languageSwitcherHint: switcher renders a dropdown in the header. Keep options in sync with the slot text.
code-block.tabsHint: tabs replaces the dropdown with a segmented control. Do not pass both unless you want tabs to win.
code-block.openInV0Hint: v0 adds a toolbar action. ask opens the snippet as a question. build prefixes the prompt with Build this.
code-block.bestPractice1: Use {codeBlock} for multi-line source. One token (path, flag, env name) stays inline. A copyable shell command is {snippet}.
code-block.bestPractice2: Always set {language} (or the {syntax} alias). Highlighting covers {vue}, {ts}, {js}, {tsx}, {html}, {css}, {bash}, {json}, and {lua}.
code-block.bestPractice3: Show {filename} when the reader has a paste destination. Drop it for throwaway examples.
code-block.bestPractice4: Highlight the few lines you are talking about. Added and removed rows belong on the dedicated number props, not in comments.
code-block.bestPractice5: Keep snippets runnable. Do not wrap shell in {dollar} — that is Snippet's job.
code-block.bestPractice6: Put the source in the default slot as text. The block reads slot text for copy and highlighting; do not nest interactive nodes inside it.

collapse.title: Collapse
collapse.description: A heading that reveals related content. Stack several in CollapseGroup for an accordion.
collapse.defaultHint: Inside a group, opening one panel closes the others.
collapse.expandedHint: defaultExpanded opens a panel on mount. In a single-select group, only the first such panel stays open.
collapse.multipleHint: multiple lets independent panels stay open together.
collapse.smallHint: small is 13px with tighter padding. Use it in dense settings, not as page structure.
collapse.controlledHint: Pass expanded and listen for update:expanded when the parent owns the open state. The title slot replaces the title prop.
collapse.previewTokenAnswer: A token authenticates API calls for one project. Rotate it if it leaks.
collapse.previewTokenAnswerShort: A token authenticates API calls for one project.
collapse.previewTokenStorageAnswer: Only the hash is stored. The plaintext value is shown once at creation.
collapse.previewTokenStorageAnswerShort: Only the hash is stored. The plaintext value is shown once.
collapse.previewReadAccessBody: List projects, deployments, and usage. Cannot mutate.
collapse.previewWriteAccessBody: Create tokens, rotate secrets, and change project settings.
collapse.previewAdvancedSettingsBody: Payload previews and raw request bodies live here. Most visits can skip this.
collapse.previewRetentionBody: Logs older than 30 days are dropped. Export before then.
collapse.practiceHideOptional: Collapse hides optional or repetitive content (FAQ, advanced settings, payload preview). Primary page structure stays as normal headings.
collapse.practiceOneBlockBefore: One optional block is a lone Collapse. A related set goes in
collapse.practiceOneBlockAfter: . Sibling views of the same data are Tabs.
collapse.practiceDefaultClosedBefore: Default closed unless the first visit cannot act without the body. In a group, skip
collapse.practiceTitleCaseBefore: Title Case the heading and name the topic, not the action —
collapse.practiceNoNest: Do not nest Collapse more than one level. Do not bury a primary destructive action inside a closed panel.

colors.title: Colors
colors.description: High-contrast scales for a black canvas. Click a swatch to copy var(--ds-…).
colors.howScaleWorksHint: Each hue uses the same 100–1000 ladder. Gray Alpha is for hairlines on both themes.

combobox.title: Combobox
combobox.description: Type to filter a known list, then pick one value. Use Select when the list is short and typing adds nothing.
combobox.controlledHint: v-model is the Vue path. value plus {'@change'} (or onChange) stay for Hesoyam-shaped call sites.
combobox.sizesHint: small is 24px, medium is 32px, large is 40px. default matches medium.
combobox.clearableHint: clearable shows a clear control after a value is selected.
combobox.widthHint: width sizes the input in pixels. maxWidth on the list lets long option text grow instead of wrapping to the input.
combobox.regionWashingtonDetail: Washington, D.C. — US East, default for this workspace.
combobox.regionFrankfurtDetail: Frankfurt — EU Central, lowest latency for this workspace.
combobox.regionSydneyDetail: Sydney — APAC South, use when the origin is in Australia.
combobox.emptyMessageHint: Override the default No items match “query” copy when the empty state needs a noun.
combobox.withLabelHint: Combobox has no label prop. Pair a Label with the same id, or set aria-label on the root.
combobox.multilineHint: ignoreDefaultHeight drops the fixed 32px row so a name plus meta can stack. The list still scrolls.
combobox.bpKnownList: Combobox filters a known list (regions, frameworks, env names). A short fixed list is Select. More than one value is Multi Select. A free-form query is Search Input.
combobox.bpLabelBefore: Visible label is a short Title Case noun. Placeholder is the hint —
combobox.bpLabelMiddle: — not a repeat of the label and not a bare
combobox.bpEmptyBefore: Empty copy should name the collection:
combobox.bpEmptyAfter: when the default is too generic.
combobox.bpEnter: Do not submit the surrounding form on Enter while the list is open. Arrow keys move, Enter selects, Escape closes.
combobox.bpErroredBefore: only paints the border. Put the constraint in a sentence under the field:
combobox.bpPrefixSuffix: Prefix and suffix accept a slot or a {prefix} / {suffix} prop. Prefer the slot with {icon}.

context-card.title: Context Card
context-card.description: A floating card on hover or focus. Use it for entity metadata that is heavier than a tooltip.
context-card.sidesDescription: Default side is top. The card flips if it would collide with the viewport.
context-card.alignmentDescription: align pins the card to the start, center, or end of the trigger. Default is center.
context-card.richContentDescription: The content slot replaces the content string when the card needs a heading and metadata rows.
context-card.customElementDescription: render (or as) changes the trigger tag. Default is a div. as-child merges behavior onto the child instead.
context-card.alignContent: {align} alignment pins the card to that edge of the trigger.
context-card.demoDefaultWrapperContent: Default wrapper is a div. as-child paints the card on the button itself.
context-card.bestPractice1: Context Card is for entity metadata on a name, avatar, or id in a dense row. One-line “why” is Tooltip. Long-form edit or navigation is a Drawer or a page.
context-card.bestPractice2a: Open delay is 150ms and close delay is 100ms on
context-card.bestPractice2b: . Keep that pause so a fast pointer sweep does not flash cards.
context-card.bestPractice3a: Lead with the entity name, then one identifying line, then two to four
context-card.bestPractice3b: rows. Unknown values use an em dash, not
context-card.bestPractice4: At most one primary action in the card. More than that is a Menu. Never put a destructive confirm in a hover surface — it can dismiss before commit.
context-card.bestPractice5: Do not nest a Context Card inside a Tooltip or another card. The trigger keeps its own accessible name; the card is supplementary.
context-card.bestPractice6c: are for composing your own trigger and delays.

context-menu.title: Context Menu
context-menu.description: Actions for the thing under the pointer. Opens on right-click or long-press. Never the only way to reach an action.
context-menu.disabledItemsDescription: disabled keeps the row visible and skips activation. Explain the lock elsewhere — a Tooltip on the row, or helper text in a Menu.
context-menu.linkItemsDescription: href renders the row as an anchor. Use it when the action changes the URL.
context-menu.bestPractice1: Context Menu is a shortcut on a row, file, or canvas object. Mirror every item on a visible Menu or row button so keyboard and mouse-only users keep parity.
context-menu.bestPractice2: A dropdown from a visible trigger is Menu. A global jump list is a command palette, not this component.
context-menu.bestPractice3d: . A trailing ellipsis means a follow-up dialog.
context-menu.bestPractice4a: Put destructive items last. Do not ship a bare
context-menu.bestPractice4b: . One level of items; nested submenus make keyboard travel unpredictable.
context-menu.bestPractice5: Bind right-click on desktop and long-press on touch, only on the trigger, not the whole page. Close on activate, Escape, or outside click — not on hover-out.
context-menu.bestPractice6b: switches the row to a link. Prefix and suffix accept a slot or a component prop.

copy-button.title: Copy Button
copy-button.description: Copies a string to the clipboard and swaps to a check while the write succeeds.
copy-button.besideHint: The control is icon-only. Sit it next to the string it copies and keep the aria-label specific.
copy-button.controlledHint: Pass copied when the parent owns the check. Uncontrolled mode resets after two seconds and still emits copy.
copy-button.bpPayload: {textToCopy} is the clipboard payload. The visible label next to the button can be a truncated or masked form of the same value.
copy-button.bpLabel: {label} becomes {ariaLabel}. Default is {copy}. Prefer {copyDeploymentId} when more than one copy control shares the view.
copy-button.bpCopied: Leave {copied} unset for the built-in two-second check. Control it only when success must stay visible or sync with another surface.
copy-button.bpDisable: Disable when there is nothing to copy yet (empty field, hidden secret). Do not disable after a successful copy.
copy-button.bpRelated: A whole command line with a prompt glyph is {snippet}. A highlighted source file is {codeBlock} — both already embed this button.
copy-button.bpIcon: The icon is decorative. Do not add a visible “Copied” word next to it; the check is the feedback.

drawer.title: Drawer
drawer.description: A bottom sheet that takes over a small viewport. Bind show and dismiss together.
drawer.callout: This port is a bottom sheet at every breakpoint so the API is visible here. In product chrome, pair it with Modal or Sheet on desktop instead of forcing a sheet on a wide screen.
drawer.defaultHint: v-model:show drives visibility. Overlay tap, Escape, and a downward drag on the handle all dismiss.
drawer.filterLogsBody: Narrow the stream to a host, status, or time range.
drawer.heightHint: height is pixels. customHeight accepts a number or a CSS length when the default frame clips the primary action.
drawer.quickFiltersBody: A short sheet. Keep Cancel and the primary action above the fold.
drawer.verticalScrollHint: vertical-scroll confines overflow to the body so the page behind the sheet does not move.
drawer.scrollEvent: Event {n} — replica health and request volume for this window.
drawer.bp1: Drawer is a mobile sheet: one form, a filter set, or a single primary action plus Cancel. Wide viewports should open Modal or Sheet instead.
drawer.bp2: Do not confirm deletes or revokes here. The overlay is a dim, not a hard block — use Modal when the action is destructive.
drawer.bp3: {drawerTitle} names the view in Title Case ({filterLogs}, {deploymentDetails}), not the page heading. Body copy stays sentence case.
drawer.bp4: Leave tap-outside, Escape, and swipe-down dismiss on. Disable them only while a form is dirty and you need to confirm discard.
drawer.bp5: Pass {verticalScroll} when the body can overflow the frame. Cap height with {height} or {customHeight} only if the CTA would otherwise sit below the fold.
drawer.bp6: {onDismiss} and {dismiss} are the same close path as {vModelShow}. Prefer the model in new Vue code.

empty-state.title: Empty State
empty-state.description: Explain why a region has no rows and what the next action is.
empty-state.blankSlateHint: First visit to a resource that has never been created. Title is Title Case. Description adds a next step.
empty-state.previewNoDeploymentsDesc: Push to your Git repository to create your first one.
empty-state.informationalHint: Default slot is the action row. One primary Button, optional secondary ButtonLink. Never three CTAs.
empty-state.previewNoProjectsDesc: Create a project to deploy previews, inspect logs, and invite the team.
empty-state.noResultsHint: A filter or search returned zero rows. Quote a single query. Offer a clear way back to the full list.
empty-state.previewNoLogsMatchFilterDesc: No logs match “production”. Clear the filter to see all logs.
empty-state.slotsHint: title, description, and icon also accept slots when the copy is not a plain string.
empty-state.previewNoTeamMembersDesc: Invite a teammate to share deployments and logs.
empty-state.bestPractice1: Pick the story by cause: blank slate for a resource that does not exist yet, no-results after a filter, permission when the route is gated, error when a load failed.
empty-state.bestPractice2: {emptyStateIcon} is the framed glyph. Put {iconComponent} in its default slot. The {iconProp} prop also accepts a Lucide component if you are not using a slot.
empty-state.bestPractice3: Title Case on the title. Sentence case on the description, and do not restate the title. CTA labels are Title Case Verb + Noun — not Get Started or OK.
empty-state.bestPractice4: One primary action. A second control is fine when the first step is genuinely a fork (Import Repository vs Deploy Template).
empty-state.bestPractice5: Persistent warnings do not belong here. They disappear when the list fills — use Note or the page header.
empty-state.bestPractice6: After an async filter change, wrap the region in {ariaLive} so the new state is announced.

entity.title: Entity
entity.description: A row with optional left media, a title and description, and a right-side control.
entity.defaultHint: left and right are slots (or render props). EntityContent holds the title and secondary line.
entity.listHint: EntityList is a divided stack. Set as="li" on each row so the markup matches the list.
entity.checkboxHint: Put the Checkbox in the left slot. Label it with the entity name so the row is selectable without relying on nearby text.
entity.fillHint: fill makes EntityContent grow so a trailing column can sit on the right edge.
entity.skeletonHint: Reserve the row while data resolves. Do not flash an empty Entity and swap it later.
entity.columnClassesHint: left-class-name and right-class-name style the side columns without wrapping extra markup.
entity.previewDashedColumns: Dashed columns mark the left and right slots.
entity.bestPractice1: Entity is a descriptive row with one or two controls: members, sessions, domains, integrations. Sortable columns belong in Table. Static key/value blocks belong in a description list.
entity.bestPractice2After: when the whole row is the control. Do not nest a Checkbox inside a button row.
entity.bestPractice3Before: Right column holds at most two actions. Anything else goes in a Menu. Labels stay Verb + Noun (
entity.bestPractice4: Lead with a scannable mark — Avatar or icon — then a Title Case name and sentence-case metadata.
entity.bestPractice5After: props accept a vnode or component for render functions. Templates should use the slots.

error.title: Error
error.description: Inline failure copy. Exported as HesoyamError so it does not collide with the built-in Error constructor.
error.defaultHint: Default label is Error. The default slot is the message. role="alert" is already on the root.
error.previewEmailInUse: This email address is already in use.
error.noLabelHint: Pass :label="false" when the surrounding field already names the problem.
error.sizesHint: small is 12px, medium is 13px, large is 16px. medium is the default.
error.errorObjectHint: error.message fills the slot when you do not pass children. action is plain text unless link is set.
error.bestPractice1: {hesoyamError} is a line of copy next to a field or under a section, not a full-page boundary. Toasts cover transient save failures. Input's own error state covers a single invalid field.
error.bestPractice2: Say what happened, then what to do. Skip "Oops", "Unfortunately", and "Unable to". User-state errors use Couldn't; system errors use Failed to.
error.bestPractice3: Name the resource ({example}), not Something Went Wrong. Pair platform failures with a stable request or deployment id the user can copy.
error.bestPractice4: {labelFalse} when a nearby Label already identifies the field. A custom {label} is for a named subsystem (Email Error, Billing Error).
error.bestPractice5: The folder also exports {error} and the legacy {geistError} name as aliases of {hesoyamError}. New pages should import {hesoyamError}.
error.bestPractice6: When the message appears after a failed request, wrap it in {ariaLive}. The component already sets {roleAlert}.

fieldset.title: Fieldset
fieldset.description: A bordered settings card: title, body, optional footer status, and footer actions.
fieldset.defaultHint: FieldsetContent is the padded body. FieldsetFooter splits status on the left and actions on the right.
fieldset.typesHint: type changes the border: default, error, warning. Use it for a section-level outcome, not a single invalid input.
fieldset.disabledHint: disabled on FieldsetContent greys the body. highlight on FieldsetFooter paints the amber permission strip.
fieldset.errorWarningHint: ErrorText and WarningText sit inside the body for a check that failed or a side effect of saving.
fieldset.disabledWallHint: DisabledWall is an absolute overlay. The parent must be relative. Pair it with a highlighted footer that states the upgrade or permission.
fieldset.withoutFooterHint: A read-only block can stop at FieldsetContent. Status-only footers omit FieldsetFooterActions.

file-tree.title: File Tree
file-tree.description: A nested directory: expandable Folder rows and File leaves, indented by depth.
file-tree.defaultHint: Tree provides depth. Folder toggles its children. default-open expands a branch on first paint.
file-tree.fileTypesHint: type is edge-function, lambda, or middleware. Each paints a badge and a tinted icon.
file-tree.linksHint: href turns the file row into an anchor. Use it when the name should open a source file or docs page.
file-tree.practice1: File Tree illustrates a layout in docs or a deploy artifact. It is not a full IDE explorer — no multi-select, rename, or drag.
file-tree.practice2After: . Depth indent comes from provide/inject; a Folder or File rendered alone sits at the root.

gauge.title: Gauge
gauge.description: Circular 0–100 readout. Pair it with a name; the ring is not self-describing.
gauge.sizesHint: tiny is 20px, small 32px, medium 64px, large 96px. Default is medium.
gauge.valueHint: show-value prints the rounded percent. tiny places the number beside the ring; other sizes draw it in the center.
gauge.defaultColorScaleHint: Without colors, the fill steps red → amber → green at 0 / 33 / 66.
gauge.customColorRangeHint: Pass a numeric scale. The stroke uses the last key the value has reached.
gauge.namedColorsHint: primary and secondary pin both arcs instead of using the threshold scale.
gauge.arcPriorityHint: equal sizes both arcs so a 50/50 ratio reads as a split. Default primary grows the filled arc only.
gauge.indeterminateHint: Spins the ring while a value is still being computed. value still sets how much of the ring is painted.
gauge.overlayHint: Default slot sits in the center. Use it for an icon, not a unit string.
gauge.bestPractice1: Gauge is a 0–100 ratio against a known max — quota, cache hit rate, uptime. Known-total task progress belongs on Progress. Binary state belongs on Badge or Status Dot.
gauge.bestPractice2: {arcPriorityEqual} for true ratios so 50% is half the ring. Leave the default {primary} when only the filled share matters.
gauge.bestPractice3: Reuse product thresholds in {colors}. Do not invent gauge-only breakpoints.
gauge.bestPractice4: Name the metric next to the ring. {showValue} prints the number only — never a {percent} or unit inside the slot.
gauge.bestPractice5: Pair {indeterminate} with copy such as «{calculatingUsage}» so a spinning ring is not read as zero.
gauge.bestPractice6: The control already sets {roleProgressbar} and value ARIA. Do not override those; color is not enough without text.

grid.title: Grid
grid.description: Two-dimensional layout with visible guides. Wrap every Grid in GridSystem.
grid.emptyGridHint: columns and rows are numbers. height preserve-aspect-ratio keeps the cell math square.
grid.cellsHint: GridCell auto-flows when column and row are omitted.
grid.solidCellsHint: solid paints a background so guides do not show through a tile. column and row accept CSS grid lines such as 1/3.
grid.responsiveHint: columns, rows, and cell spans can be {'{ sm, md, lg }'}. Breakpoints are 600px and 960px. unstable_use-container measures the wrapper, not the viewport.
grid.responsiveSpansHint: A solid cell can change its line range per breakpoint.
grid.hiddenGuidesHint: hide-guides is row or column — not both. Hiding both means a plain Tailwind grid is enough.
grid.overlappingCellsHint: Explicit line ranges can stack. Later cells paint above earlier ones.
grid.crossesHint: GridCross marks an intersection. column and row are 1-based guide indices, including the trailing edge.
grid.debugHint: debug outlines the system and every cell so span math is visible while you author.
grid.overlapLorem: Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit.
grid.bestPractice1: Use Grid when the guides are part of the design — marketing bands, docs landings, feature tiles. Plain cards and lists should stay on Tailwind {grid}.
grid.bestPractice2: Always wrap in {gridSystem}. Docs and embeds should set {unstableUseContainer} so {sm} / {md} / {lg} follow the wrapper width.
grid.bestPractice3: Set columns and rows at all three breakpoints when the layout reflows. One number is fine for a fixed frame.
grid.bestPractice4: {solid} on a cell that needs an opaque tile. Without it, guides draw through the content.
grid.bestPractice5: Do not nest Grid more than one level. Guide overlap turns into noise and the cell math breaks.
grid.bestPractice6: {gridPage} is a full-viewport shell ({minHDvh}). Keep it off this docs canvas; use it as a page root.
grid.bestPractice7: Guides are decorative. Put semantics on the cell content. If a cell is tappable, give it its own focus ring.

icon-tile.title: Icon Tile
icon-tile.description: A 22px icon well with an inner glass stroke. Use it to mark a row in a nav or settings list.
icon-tile.colorsHint: Eight tones on design tokens. Each fill is a 135deg ramp around the source hex — not a flat color.
icon-tile.fromHexHint: Pass color as a hex. The source sits in the middle of the ramp: #9D9DA4 becomes #ADADB4 to #8E8E95.
icon-tile.sizesHint: small is 22px — the nav default. medium is 28px, large is 32px.
icon-tile.themeSyncHint: Pass theme-sync to follow light and dark. Light keeps the colored well and white glyph. Dark switches to a graphite plate with a colored glyph.
icon-tile.inListHint: Pair the tile with a label. Keep one tile per row; do not stack them as a filter group.
icon-tile.bestPractice1: Pass a Lucide component through icon. Keep the glyph at the size IconTile already sets — do not wrap a second Icon at 24px.
icon-tile.bestPractice2: small is for sidebars and dense lists. Jump to medium or large only when the tile is the primary mark on a card or empty row.
icon-tile.bestPractice3: Pick a tone that stays distinct from its neighbors. Repeating blue on every row removes the scan value.
icon-tile.bestPractice4: The glass stroke is decorative. Do not add an extra border or drop shadow around the tile.
icon-tile.bestPractice5: For a custom fill, pass color as hex. Do not set background-image yourself — iconTileGradientFromHex already builds the ramp.
icon-tile.bestPractice6: Use theme-sync in nav and settings rows so dark appearance gets the graphite plate. Leave it off when the tile should stay a colored well in both appearances.

icons.title: Icons
icons.description: Lucide for this port. Import named icons from {core} and render with {icon}.
icons.importCallout: Use {icon} in product UI so size and stroke stay consistent.
icons.sizesHint: Match the control. 14px on h-8, 12px on meta rows, 32px only inside EmptyStateIcon.

input.title: Input
input.description: Single-line text. Use Textarea when the value can wrap, Combobox when it comes from a known list.
input.sizesHint: Default in this port is 40px (also aliased as medium). small is 32px, large is 48px.
input.prefixAndSuffixHint: String addons, icon slots, or both. prefix-styling and suffix-styling drop the tinted rail.
input.errorHint: error paints the border red and renders the message under the field.
input.label: Label
input.labelHint: Passing label renders Label above the field and wires html-for for you.
input.roundedHint: rounded makes a pill. Pair it with prefix / suffix for domain-style fields.
input.bp1: One line of free-form text: names, domains, tokens. Multi-line → Textarea. Filter a known list → Combobox. Inline search → Search Input, not this field inside another form.
input.bp2: Validate on blur. Pass a sentence to {error}: "Project name is required." Skip "please".
input.bp3: Labels are short Title Case nouns. Placeholders are example values ({exampleCom}), never instructions.
input.bp4: Keep the field focusable while saving. {disabled} only when typing is impossible.
input.bp5: {sizeMedium} matches {sizeDefault} (40px). New code can use either; product chrome often wants {sizeSmall}.
input.bp6: Bind with {vmodel}. Native attributes ({type}, {placeholder}, {autocomplete}) fall through to the inner {input}.

installation.title: Installation
installation.description: Source-distributed Vue 3 kit. Tailwind has to scan the shipped components.
installation.sourceHint: The package is source, not a prebuilt bundle. A compiled dist would strip the Tailwind utilities that live inside the {vue} files.
installation.peersHint: The second line is the peer set. If Vue and Tailwind are already in the app, add only reka-ui and {'@lucide/vue'}.
installation.nuxtHint: The module auto-imports components, injects the theme into the Tailwind entry stylesheet, and keeps the package out of Vite pre-bundling.
installation.nuxtOptionsHint: Defaults are empty prefix, auto-import on, theme on.
installation.optionComponents: {components}: auto-import. Set false to import by hand.
installation.optionTheme: {theme}: inject {css} after the Tailwind import. If that file already imports the theme, the module leaves it alone.
installation.viteHint: Import the theme from the same stylesheet as Tailwind. Tell Vite not to pre-bundle the package — esbuild cannot process the .vue files it ships.
installation.globalHint: A Vue plugin if you want every component on the app instance.
installation.themeHint: theme.css defines the --ds-* scales, type, radius, and the {'@source'} rules that let Tailwind see the components. Override tokens after the import.
installation.fontsHint: Typography expects Geologica ({sans}) and Geist Mono ({mono}). Both fall back to system fonts if you do not load them.
installation.importsHint: Named exports from the barrel, or a folder if you prefer not to go through the index.
installation.practice1: Never pre-bundle the package. The Nuxt module already adds {exclude}. Vite apps must set it by hand.
installation.practice2: Import the theme from the stylesheet that imports Tailwind. A second CSS file will not scan the components.
installation.practice3: Dark mode is a {dark} class on a parent, usually html. The dark palette is the reference; light is the adaptation.
installation.practice4: Typecheck with {vueTsc} or Volar. Plain {tsc} cannot type .vue source.
installation.practice5: Node 20.19 or newer. Nuxt 3.13+ or Vue 3.5+.

keyboard-input.title: Keyboard Input
keyboard-input.description: Shortcut hint. Kbd swaps glyphs for the current OS — do not hard-code ⌘.
keyboard-input.modifiersHint: Boolean props render the platform key. Apple gets Command / Control / Option / Shift glyphs; other platforms get Ctrl, Alt, and Shift.
keyboard-input.combinationHint: Stack modifiers, then put the trigger key in the default slot.
keyboard-input.smallHint: Use small inside menus, command rows, and table cells.
keyboard-input.bestPractice1: Shortcut chips in UI chrome: menus, button suffixes, empty states. Long-form docs that narrate a shortcut can write the glyphs in text so a copy stays readable.
keyboard-input.bestPractice2: Pass {meta}, {shift}, {alt}, {ctrl}. Hard-coding {cmdK} is wrong on Windows and Linux.
keyboard-input.bestPractice3: Children are one key: {k}, {seven}, {enter}, {esc}. Do not lowercase, do not spell modifiers in the slot.
keyboard-input.bestPractice4: Punctuation stays outside the element. “Press K to open the command menu.” — the period is not a key.
keyboard-input.bestPractice5: {keyboardInput} is the same export as {kbd}. New code should import {kbdImport}.

label.title: Label
label.description: Accessible name for a form control. Title-cases value unless you opt out.
label.defaultHint: value is the visible text. The control association is html-for, matching the native for attribute.
label.withInputHint: with-input adds space under the label. Point html-for at the field id.
label.bypassCasingHint: value is Title Cased by default («email address» → «Email Address»). bypass-casing keeps the string you pass.
label.slotHint: Default slot replaces value when you need markup inside the label.
label.onInputHint: Input already mounts Label when you pass label. Use this component when the label sits elsewhere or needs extra markup.
label.practiceVisibleLabel: Every text field, select, and checkbox needs a visible Label. Placeholder is not a name.
label.practiceHtmlFor: Wire {htmlFor} to the control {id}. A matching {id} on the Label itself is only for {ariaLabelledby}.
label.practiceShortCopy: Keep copy to a short Title Case noun: Project Name, Domain, Environment Variable. Helper sentences live next to the field, not in the label.
label.practiceBypassCasing: Use {bypassCasing} for product names, env keys, and any string that is not English title case.
label.practicePreferInput: Prefer {input}'s {label} prop for a stacked field. Use Label directly when the caption is shared, sits beside the control, or contains extra markup.

loading-dots.title: Loading Dots
loading-dots.description: Indeterminate wait inside a line of copy. Buttons use their own loading prop instead.
loading-dots.sizesHint: Named sizes are sm (4px), md (6px), and lg (8px). Default is md. A number is the dot diameter in pixels.
loading-dots.withTextHint: Default slot renders before the dots. Name the work that is still running.
loading-dots.colorHint: Dots use currentColor. Change the wrapper text color to retint them.
loading-dots.bestPractice1: Short waits inside a sentence: Saving, Building, Deploying. Layout placeholders → Skeleton. Known progress → Progress. Icon-sized waits → Spinner.
loading-dots.bestPractice2: Do not drop dots into a Button label. Set {loading} on Button so the control stays the same size and remains focusable.
loading-dots.bestPractice3: The trailing word names the work still in flight. {saved} plus dots is a contradiction.
loading-dots.bestPractice4: The root already has {ariaLive}. Meaning lives in the slot text; do not add a second {ariaLabel} on the dots.
loading-dots.bestPractice5: Pass a numeric {size} only when a named size misses the adjacent type. One animated indicator per row.

marquee.title: Marquee
marquee.description: An infinite ticker with Scroller-style edge fades. Hover pauses the motion.
marquee.defaultHint: Slot chips, logos, or a line of copy. Extra copies fill the rail so the loop has no seam.
marquee.reverseHint: reverse runs the rail the other way.
marquee.durationHint: duration is seconds for one copy to travel its own width. Smaller is faster. Default is 40.
marquee.pauseOnHoverHint: pause-on-hover is on by default. Set it false only when the row is decorative and never contains a control.
marquee.textHint: A single line of copy also works. Keep it one sentence.
marquee.textCopy: Deploy preview is live · Checks passed · Promote when ready
marquee.bestPractice1: Use Marquee for logos, status chips, or a short announcement rail — not for a list the user must read in order.
marquee.bestPractice2: Keep {pauseOnHover} on when the slot has links or buttons so a pointer can hit the target.
marquee.bestPractice3: Fades sit on both edges automatically. Do not add a second mask or box-shadow.
marquee.bestPractice4: Tune speed with {duration}, not a custom keyframe. Keep item widths and the gap even so the loop does not hitch.
marquee.bestPractice5: {reducedMotion} stops the animation. Do not re-enable it.
marquee.bestPractice6: Duplicate nodes are aria-hidden. Put the real content in the default slot once.

menu.bestPractice3b: and sit last, under a divider.

modal.description: A blocking dialog for a decision the page cannot continue without.
modal.defaultHint: Bind open state with v-model:active. active and open are aliases.
modal.tokenSubtitle: Enter a unique name so you can tell this token apart later.

modal.stickyLine6: Expiration is a date, not a reminder.

modal.stickyLine8: Revoke unused tokens instead of leaving them idle.
modal.insetHint: ModalInset is a recessed band for a field or a preview. last drops the bottom border when it sits on the actions.
modal.insetSubtitle: The inset holds the field. Copy outside it stays on the page background.
modal.inviteEmailHint: They will get an email with a link to join this team.
modal.disabledAndFullWidthHint: Disable the primary until the form is valid. full-width stretches a single acknowledgment action.
modal.submitDisabledHint: Submit stays disabled until the name is unique.
modal.copyNowHint: Copy it now. This value is not shown again.
modal.initialFocusHint: initial-focus-ref moves first focus onto a control. Pass a component instance or an HTMLElement.
modal.focusHint: Focus lands on Create Token so Enter continues without a Tab.

modal.bp2Before: Title is Title Case and a statement:

multi-select.description: Pick several values from one field. Each row can isolate itself or restore the full set.

multi-select.alignHint: MultiSelectContent align is start by default. end lines the menu up with the trailing edge of the trigger.

note.title: Note
note.description: Inline guidance that stays in the page flow. Not a toast and not a modal.

note.sizesHint: medium is the default. small fits toolbars, sidebars, and dense forms.
note.previewBandwidth: Bandwidth resets on the first of the month.
note.label: Label
note.labelHint: NoteLabel is a leading strong word. Keep it one or two words, then the sentence.
note.previewChangesApply: Changes apply to new deployments only.
note.previewBuildExceeded: The build exceeded the log limit.
note.actionHint: NoteAction sits on the trailing edge. One small Button. Do not put a second CTA in the copy.
