pagination.title: Pagination
pagination.description: Previous and next links for a linear docs or settings sequence. Not a numbered page list.
pagination.defaultDescription: Pass previous and next as {'{ title, href }'}. Either side may be omitted.
pagination.bestPractice1: This control is for a path the user walks in order — docs, onboarding, a wizard. A table with many pages needs a different pattern.
pagination.bestPractice2After: is the destination page name, Title Case, not “Previous page”. The word Previous / Next is already in the chrome.
pagination.bestPractice3: Omit the side that does not exist. Do not invent a disabled link back to the same URL.
pagination.bestPractice4: Keep titles short enough to truncate cleanly. The row caps each side at half the width.
pagination.bestPractice5After: should be a real route. This component renders anchors, not buttons, so it is for navigation only.

progress.title: Progress
progress.description: A determinate bar for a known percent. Not a spinner and not a gauge.
progress.defaultHint: value and model-value are aliases. max defaults to 100.
progress.typesHint: type locks the fill to a status color. Use it when the meaning is already known.
progress.colorsHint: colors is a threshold map: the fill uses the last key the percent has crossed.
progress.stopsHint: stops draw ticks on the track. tooltip wraps each tick. aria-label is used when there is no tooltip.
progress.sizeHint: Default height is 4px. width and height accept a number (px) or any CSS length.
progress.bestPractice1: Progress is for a known fraction: upload, quota, a build step with a percent. An unknown wait is Spinner or Loading Dots. A score is Gauge.
progress.bestPractice2: Pair the bar with visible numbers nearby — {example}. The bar alone is not a value.
progress.bestPractice3: {type} is a fixed status. {colors} is for a bar that changes meaning as it fills, such as quota headroom.
progress.bestPractice4: Stops mark policy thresholds, not decoration. Give each one a tooltip the user can read on hover.
progress.bestPractice5: Do not animate the value yourself on every frame. Pass the latest percent and let the indicator transition.

radio.title: Radio
radio.description: Pick one value from a short, visible set. Switch in this port is a segmented control — use Radio for classic radio buttons.
radio.callout: Bind the group with {vModel} or {value}. {switch} is not an on/off toggle here; that control is {toggle}.
radio.defaultHint: RadioGroup renders a fieldset. RadioGroupItem wraps each option in a label.
radio.disabledHint: disabled on the group locks every option. On an item it greys out one choice.
radio.requiredHint: Put required on RadioGroup, not on a single item. Native constraint validation then blocks submit.
radio.headlessHint: useRadio returns a Radio bound to a value so you can own the label layout.
radio.standaloneHint: Bare Radio for custom rows. It needs an accessible name and you own checked state.
radio.practice1: Two to six mutually exclusive choices that should stay on screen. Past that, use {select} or {combobox}.
radio.practice2: On/off is {toggle}. Two or three compact peers in a pill is {switch}. Radio is the circular control.
radio.practice3: Pre-select the safe default so the field looks configured. Leave it empty only when the pick has real consequences.
radio.practice4: Group label is a Title Case noun ({deploymentRegion}). Option labels stay parallel: {monthly} / {yearly}.
radio.practice5: {required} belongs on {radioGroup}. A single required radio is meaningless.
radio.practice6: A disabled option needs a reason nearby. A grey circle with no copy reads as broken.
radio.practice7: Standalone {radio} always gets {ariaLabel} or a wired {label}.

scroller.title: Scroller
scroller.description: A clipped list with edge fades. Optional buttons jump to the next direct child.
scroller.verticalHint: overflow='y' is the default. Pass height as a number (px) or a CSS string.
scroller.horizontalHint: Set overflow='x' and keep the rail wider than the viewport.
scroller.bothHint: overflow='both' when the canvas really moves on two axes — long log lines, maps of tiles.
scroller.verticalWithButtonsHint: with-buttons scrolls the next or previous direct child into view. Do not wrap items in an extra layout node.
scroller.bestPractice1: Use Scroller for a peer list that overflows one axis: chip rails, log streams, snippet stacks.
scroller.bestPractice2: {y} for feeds, {x} for tiles. {both} only when content truly scrolls in two directions.
scroller.bestPractice3: Button targets are direct children of the slot. An extra wrapper makes the arrows jump the whole block.
scroller.bestPractice4: Keep horizontal item widths and gaps even so the rail does not feel ragged.
scroller.bestPractice5: Fades appear on the clipped edges automatically. Do not add a second shadow on top.
scroller.bestPractice6: Huge lists belong in a virtualizer inside the scroller, not as hundreds of raw nodes.

search-input.title: Search Input
search-input.description: Input prewired with a search glyph, clear control, and Escape-to-empty.
search-input.defaultHint: Default size is 40px. Prefix is the search icon; a value reveals the clear button.
search-input.sizesHint: small is 32px. default and medium are 40px. large is 48px.
search-input.commandHintDescription: cmdk swaps the clear button for a Meta+K chip. After typing it becomes Esc.
search-input.loadingHint: loading replaces the suffix with a spinner so in-flight search stays obvious.
search-input.customPrefixHint: Override the magnifier with the prefix slot. Icons still come from {'@lucide/vue'}.
search-input.bp1: Always pass {ariaLabel} or a visible label. The glyph is decoration.
search-input.bp2: Placeholder is a short action, not the field name restated. {searchProjects}, not {search} again.
search-input.bp3: Keep {loading} on while results are in flight. Do not swap the whole field for a spinner.
search-input.bp4: {cmdk} is for command palettes. Ordinary filters should keep the clear button.
search-input.bp5: Escape already clears. Do not bind a second Escape handler that fights it.
search-input.bp6: Use {input} when the field is not search. This wrapper is only the search chrome.

select.title: Select
select.description: Native dropdown for a short, fixed list. Default size in this port is medium (32px).
select.sizesHint: small is 24px, medium is 32px, large is 40px. size='default' falls through to medium.
select.withOptionsHint: v-model or default-value. Children are native option and optgroup nodes.
select.labelAndRequiredHint: label renders above the control. required adds the red asterisk and the native constraint.
select.errorHint: Pass a sentence to error. The control turns red and the message is wired with aria-describedby.
select.bpShortLists: Short fixed lists (under ~10). Filtering belongs on {combobox}. Several values at once is {multiSelect}.
select.bpSwitchRadio: Two or three compact peers in a pill → {switch}. Two to six options that must stay visible → {radio}.
select.bpOptgroup: Group long lists with native {optgroup}. This port has no Select.Group.
select.bpLabelPlaceholder: Label is a Title Case noun ({labelExample}). Placeholder is an action ({placeholderExample}), never "Choose one…".
select.bpCanonicalSpelling: Options keep one register and canonical spelling ({nextJs}, not {nextJsBad}).
select.bpValidate: Validate on blur and pass a full sentence to {error}, ending in a period.

separator.title: Separator
separator.description: A 1px rule that splits sections. Horizontal by default, decorative so it stays out of the accessibility tree.
separator.previewSection1Copy: First block of copy in the stack.
separator.previewSection2Copy: Second block of copy in the stack.
separator.verticalHint: The parent must be a flex row with a height. The rule stretches with self-stretch.
separator.bestPractice1: Separate sibling blocks, not every line. Space plus type already groups most copy.
separator.bestPractice2: Default {decorative} is correct for visual rules. Set {decorativeFalse} only when the split is a real landmark.
separator.bestPractice3: Vertical separators need a flex parent with a height. A block parent collapses the 1px column to nothing.
separator.bestPractice4: Color is {color}. Do not recolor it per section.
separator.bestPractice5: Menus and toolbars can use a short vertical rule. Page layout uses a full-width horizontal one.

sheet.title: Sheet
sheet.description: A panel that slides in from an edge. Built on Dialog, so this port defaults to modal.
sheet.callout: Reka Dialog sets {modal} to {trueValue}. Pass {modalFalse} only when the page behind must stay interactive.
sheet.defaultHint: Trigger with as-child so the Button stays the focus target. Content defaults to the right edge.
sheet.deploymentDescription: Inspect the latest production deploy without leaving the list.
sheet.deploymentBody: Commit message, checks, and assigned domains stay here. The page behind is the list of deploys.
sheet.sideHint: side is top, right, bottom, or left. Pick from the trigger: a row inspector from the right, filters from the left.
sheet.panelFromSide: This panel slides in from the {side}.
sheet.closeControlHint: show-close-button is on by default. Turn it off when the footer already owns dismiss.
sheet.footerOwnsDismiss: Footer owns dismiss so the corner close stays hidden.
sheet.noOverlayHint: no-overlay skips the dimmer when the sheet should sit on the live page.
sheet.noOverlayDescription: The list behind stays undimmed. Use this for lightweight inspectors.
sheet.bp1: Sheet is associated context: a deploy, a member, a log row. A blocking decision is {modal}. A mobile-only bottom panel is {drawer}.
sheet.bp2: Do not confirm a delete in a sheet. Severity needs a modal that owns the screen.
sheet.bp3: Keep {side} stable for a given flow. Do not flip edges mid-session.
sheet.bp4: Title names the entity ({deploymentDetails}), not the page action. Do not repeat the page header inside.
sheet.bp5: Always ship a visible close — the corner icon or a footer {sheetClose}. Honor Escape.
sheet.bp6: Focus returns to the trigger on close. Do not steal it to the first row of the table.

show-more.title: Show More
show-more.description: Expand or collapse a long list or block. The trigger owns aria-expanded; you own the content.
show-more.defaultHint: Controlled. Toggle expanded and render the hidden rows yourself.
show-more.expandedHint: Pass expanded to flip the chevron and the default Show Less label.
show-more.noBorderHint: Drop the hairline when the trigger sits on a card or already-divided stack.
show-more.customLabelHint: Slot the label. Title Case. Include the hidden count so the click has a cost.
show-more.practice1: Use Show More for one long list or block. Sibling pages of the same set belong on Pagination. Optional sections belong on Collapse.
show-more.practice2: Show 5–10 rows before truncating so the list still has a shape. Cutting at two rows makes the control feel decorative.
show-more.practice3Before: Put the hidden count in the label (
show-more.practice4: Do not collapse the same list after the user opened it in the middle of a flow. That jumps the scroll away from what they were reading.
show-more.practice5: Keep a small hidden set in the DOM so find-in-page works. Lazy-load only when the extra rows would hurt first paint.
show-more.practice6Before: The trigger is a button. Point
show-more.practice6After: at the list. After expand, move focus to the first newly shown row.

sidebar.title: Sidebar
sidebar.description: Leftover shadcn app shell. Hesoyam has no Sidebar analog — document usage, do not invent a replacement.
sidebar.partsHint: Wrap the app in SidebarProvider. Sidebar is the rail. SidebarInset is the main column. SidebarTrigger toggles desktop collapse and the mobile sheet.
sidebar.callout: Sidebar is leftover shadcn. There is no Hesoyam navigation rail. Keep this folder for the existing shell. New chrome should reuse the current Sidebar tree, not a one-off list of links.
sidebar.propProvider: Provider: {defaultOpen} / {vModelOpen}. Cookie remembers the desktop state. {cmdB} / {ctrlB} toggles.
sidebar.propPreviewCollapsible: This preview uses {collapsibleNone} so the rail stays in flow and does not pin to the viewport.
sidebar.bp1: One SidebarProvider per shell. Nested providers fight over the same cookie and shortcut.
sidebar.bp2: Collapsed icon mode needs a {tooltip} on SidebarMenuButton — the label is clipped.
sidebar.bp3: Do not restyle the rail with a new width scale. Width tokens live on the provider.
sidebar.bp4: Mobile already becomes a Sheet. Do not wrap Sidebar in another drawer.

skeleton.title: Skeleton
skeleton.description: Reserve the layout of content that is still loading. Match the final width, height, and shape.
skeleton.boxHeightHint: box-height sets the block size. height is the fallback when box-height is omitted.
skeleton.wrappingChildrenHint: Wrap the real control to inherit its size. show (default true) paints the shimmer; show false reveals the child.
skeleton.fixedSizeHint: Lock width and height so the swap does not reflow neighbors when children resolve.
skeleton.shapesHint: pill for avatars, default rounded for buttons and chips, squared for image tiles. rounded is accepted and matches the default 6px corner.
skeleton.buttonHint: button grows the shimmer by 1px so it covers the control's border.
skeleton.bestPractice1: Skeleton is for async data that fills a known layout: rows, cards, a profile block. A single in-flight action uses Spinner or Button {loading}. Known progress uses Progress. No data at all uses Empty State.
skeleton.bestPractice2: Set {width} and {height} / {boxHeight} to the resolved content. A 200×20 block becoming an 80×16 string reads as a glitch.
skeleton.bestPractice3: Pick {pill}, default rounded, or {squared} to mirror the element that will appear.
skeleton.bestPractice4: When wrapping children, keep those dimensions stable and toggle {show}. Do not mount a different box on reveal.
skeleton.bestPractice5: Mark the loading region {ariaBusy}. Announce completion on the destination with {ariaLive}, not on the skeleton. The skeleton itself is decorative.
skeleton.bestPractice6: Turn animation off on low-power surfaces and respect {prefersReducedMotion}. Do not leave focusable controls inside a visible skeleton.

slider.title: Slider
slider.description: Pick a number from a range when shape and proximity matter more than typing a precise value.
slider.defaultHint: Value is a number array. One thumb is [n]. v-model and value are both wired.
slider.label: Label
slider.labelHint: A label plus the live value in tabular nums. Hide the live readout when start or end inputs are on.
slider.rangeWithInputsHint: Two thumbs. show-start-input and show-end-input add numeric fields that stay in range.
slider.commitOnReleaseHint: value-change fires while dragging. value-committed fires when the pointer or keyboard gesture ends.
slider.stepHint: Snap to a product increment. min and max should be real limits, not decorative ones.
slider.bestPractice1: Use a slider for ranged numbers where closeness matters: volume, opacity, bandwidth caps, color channels. Ports, memory limits, and IDs belong in an Input.
slider.bestPractice2: Always show the live value and name what it is. The track alone is not self-describing.
slider.bestPractice3: Snap with {step} so a drag never lands on {badValue}. Clamp {min} and {max} to real product bounds.
slider.bestPractice4: Pair the track with numeric inputs when the user may type. Keyboard users will.
slider.bestPractice5: Write expensive work on {valueCommitted}, not on every {valueChange}.
slider.bestPractice6: Give the control a name through {label} or {ariaLabel}. Leave arrow keys, Page Up/Down, Home, and End to the slider.

snippet.title: Snippet
snippet.description: A copyable shell command. Authors never type the leading $. The component draws the prompt.
snippet.invertedHint: dark inverts the chrome for a terminal-on-black block.
snippet.caretHint: caret draws a blinking block after the last line, like a console cursor. It is decorative and is not copied.
snippet.multiLineHint: Pass a string array. Keep it short. Longer scripts belong in Code Block.
snippet.noPromptHint: Turn the $ off for URLs, JSON, or output that must copy exactly as shown.
snippet.callbackHint: copy fires after the clipboard write. Use it for toasts or a parent checkmark.
snippet.placeholderHint: Empty text plus placeholder. The placeholder is informational and is not copied.
snippet.previewPlaceholder: Run vercel link to fetch env vars
snippet.copyTextHint: copy-text overrides the clipboard payload when the visible line is a short label.
snippet.controlledCopiedHint: Drive the checkmark from a parent when another surface copies a different payload.
snippet.bp1: Snippet is a runnable command the user is meant to copy. Inline tokens use {inlineCode}. Multi-line source uses {codeBlock}.
snippet.bp2: Pass the command as {text}. Do not prefix {dollar} yourself or the row renders {doubleDollar}.
snippet.bp3: Set {prompt} to false for non-shell strings so the visible text matches the clipboard.
snippet.bp4: One command per snippet. An array is a short sequence. Longer scripts move to {codeBlock} so people can read before they copy.
snippet.bp5: Placeholder is sentence case, no trailing period, no “Please”. It is not copied. The copy button disables when text is empty and {copyText} is unset.
snippet.bp6: Use {copyText} only when the visible line is not the payload. For a plain string, it is redundant.

spinner.title: Spinner
spinner.description: Indeterminate wait after a user action. Prefer Button loading for submits; Skeleton for a known layout.
spinner.defaultHint: md is 20px. Fading blades inherit currentColor, defaulting to gray-700.
spinner.circleHint: Pass circle for the rotating ring.
spinner.sizesHint: Named sizes map to 16, 20, 24, 32, 36, 48, and 64. A number is pixels.
spinner.colorsHint: Tint with text-* on design tokens. The glyph uses currentColor.
spinner.bestPractice1: Use Spinner for an indeterminate wait of about one to three seconds: an icon refresh, a row retry, pagination. Named sizes stay on the control, not the parent pane.
spinner.bestPractice2: On a submit control, set Button {loading}. Do not nest a Spinner inside the button by hand.
spinner.bestPractice3: Known layouts use Skeleton. Inline copy uses Loading Dots. Known totals use Progress.
spinner.bestPractice4: Mount the Spinner when the action starts. Toggling visibility on a pre-rendered spinner leaves a half-faded glyph at idle.
spinner.bestPractice5: After about a second, pair the spinner with copy that names the work: Verifying…, Deploying….
spinner.bestPractice6: Set {ariaBusy} on the in-flight region. Keep the original trigger focusable. The glyph is decorative.

split-button.title: Split Button
split-button.description: One primary action plus a menu of close variants. The first menu item must match the visible label.
split-button.sizesAndVariantsDescription: Hesoyam sizes are small, medium, large. Variants are default and secondary. sm / lg still map through.
split-button.saveRedeployDescription: Save changes and create a new production deployment
split-button.menuAlignmentDescription: bottom-start (default) lines up under the primary. bottom-end when the control sits on the right edge.
split-button.iconDescription: Slot an icon on each menu item. Keep the glyph at 16px.
split-button.titleWithIconDescription: The title slot can hold a glyph plus the verb. Description stays plain text.
split-button.bestPractice1: Use a Split Button when one action is the default and 1–4 close variants sit next to it. Unrelated actions belong in a Menu.
split-button.bestPractice2: Repeat the primary action as the first menu item. The visible label and that title must match exactly.
split-button.bestPractice3: Stay on {default} or {secondary}. Destructive work does not hide behind the chevron. {secondary2} maps to the button {outline} alias internally.
split-button.bestPractice4: Title Case every item. Verb + noun: Deploy to Production, Promote to Production. Put danger at the bottom.
split-button.bestPractice5: {menuButtonLabel} is required. It becomes the chevron's {ariaLabel} — the only name a screen reader hears for that button. Write a sentence: More deploy options.
split-button.bestPractice6: Prefer the {menuItemsSlot} slot. The {menuItemsProp} prop accepts VNodes when a parent builds the list in script.

switch.title: Switch
switch.description: Segmented control for two or three mutually exclusive views of the same surface. Not a boolean on/off.
switch.callout: {switch} + {switchControl} is a radio group in a pill. On/off settings use {toggle}. Classic circles use {radio}.
switch.defaultHint: Give the group a name so the radios stay exclusive. Mark one control defaultChecked (or bind v-model).
switch.sizesHint: small is 24px, default is 32px, large is 40px. Size on Switch flows to every control.
switch.fullWidthHint: Switch is inline-flex. Stretch it with class w-full so each control shares the row.
switch.disabledHint: disabled on Switch locks the group. On a single SwitchControl it greys out one option.
switch.iconHint: Pass a label even when the icon carries the meaning. The label is sr-only on icon-only controls.
switch.tooltipHint: Icon-only switches need a Tooltip so sighted users get the same name as the sr-only label.
switch.controlledHint: v-model (or value) on Switch. Prefer that over checked on each control.
switch.practice1Before: Two or three peers that change the view of one surface:
switch.practice2Middle: . More than three options, or labels longer than two words, become
switch.practice3After: on the group so the radios share a name. Without it, more than one pill can look selected.
switch.practice4Middle: on exactly one control, or bind
switch.practice5Before: Title Case, one or two words, parallel grammar.
switch.practice6: Size the controls so the widest label fits. A jumping pill on selection is a layout bug.

table.title: Table
table.description: Semantic HTML table. Wrap it in TableRoot so wide grids scroll instead of breaking the page.
table.basicHint: TableRoot is the overflow wrapper. Table is the table element. Header cells are TableHead, body cells are TableCell.
table.stripedHint: striped on TableBody tints even rows with --ds-gray-100.
table.borderedHint: bordered draws a hairline on every cell. Use it when columns must line up for comparison.
table.interactiveHint: interactive adds a hover wash and a pointer. You still own click and the selected row.
table.fullFeaturedHint: TableColgroup sets column widths. TableFooter sits under the body for a subtotal.
table.virtualizedHint: virtualize on TableBody pins the header and caps the root at 420px. This port scrolls the body; it does not window individual rows.
table.bestPractice1: Use a table when every row shares a shape and at least one column is comparable. A membership row with one action is an entity list, not a table. Key/value metadata is a description list.
table.bestPractice2: Wrap the grid in {tableRoot}. The table element itself should stay {table}.
table.bestPractice3: Empty lists render an Empty State outside the table, not a blank {tableBody}.
table.bestPractice4: Unknown cells are an em dash. Do not write {na}, {null}, or leave the cell empty.
table.bestPractice5: Headers are Title Case nouns: {lastUsed}, {requests7d}. Never a sentence.
table.bestPractice6: Numeric columns get {tabularNums} so digits line up.
table.bestPractice7: {interactiveProp} is a hover affordance. Wire selection and keyboard yourself.

tabs.title: Tabs
tabs.description: Switch sibling views inside one page. The component is the tablist; you render the panel.
tabs.defaultDescription: v-model binds the active value. selected + setSelected is the Hesoyam-shaped alias.
tabs.secondaryDescription: variant secondary is a compact pill. Use it in dense chrome, not as page-level navigation.
tabs.disabledDescription: disabled on Tabs locks the whole list. Pointer events drop and opacity falls to 50.
tabs.disableTabDescription: disabled + tooltip on one item. The tooltip names the constraint, not the tab's purpose.
tabs.iconsDescription: tabs[].icon is a Vue component or VNode. Build Lucide icons through Icon.
tabs.badgeDescription: badge is a count chip. Omit it at zero — do not append (12) to the title.
tabs.bestPractice1d: . Unrelated pages belong in a sub-menu.
tabs.bestPractice2: Cap the row at five to seven on desktop, three or four on mobile. Past that, fold extras into a Menu.
tabs.bestPractice3a: Two or three compact peers of the same surface stay a
tabs.bestPractice3b: . Tabs imply a larger view change.
tabs.bestPractice4: Selecting a tab is instant. Do not toast or confirm the click. Persist the value in the URL so refresh restores it.
tabs.bestPractice5b: is Title Case, one or two nouns. Verbs belong on buttons.
tabs.bestPractice6a: Disable a tab for permission or an empty state, and put the reason on
tabs.bestPractice7b: , not the title. Drop the badge at zero.
tabs.bestPractice8b: when no heading sits above it. Default is
tabs.bestPractice9: Arrows move focus. Enter and Space activate. Do not steal those keys for page shortcuts.

textarea.title: Textarea
textarea.description: Multi-line input. Use Input for a single value like a name or domain.
textarea.defaultHint: Native attrs (placeholder, rows, readonly) pass through to the textarea.
textarea.sample: Warm pool in IAD after the deploy. Sticky sessions stay on the same egress IP for 30 minutes.
textarea.samplePlaceholder: Warm pool in IAD after the deploy.
textarea.sizesHint: small is 13px. default and medium share the 14px style. large is 16px.
textarea.errorHint: Pass a string to error. The message is wired with aria-invalid and aria-describedby.
textarea.readOnlyHint: readonly is a native attr. The field stays copyable and skips the disabled wash.
textarea.rowsHint: Set rows when the surface has a fixed vertical budget. resize-y is already on the field.
textarea.commitPlaceholder: Summarize the change in one paragraph.
textarea.bp1: Multi-line content only: commit messages, descriptions, notes. A name, domain, or token is {input}.
textarea.bp2: Pick a generous default {rows}. Do not let the field push the primary action below the fold.
textarea.bp3: Validate on blur. Pass the failure string to {error} so the inline message replaces helper text.
textarea.bp4: Trim leading and trailing whitespace on submit so empty newlines do not pass {required}.
textarea.bp5: Labels are short Title Case nouns ({description}, {releaseNotes}). Placeholders show an example, not "Enter a description".
textarea.bp6: Error copy names the field and the constraint, ends with a period, and skips "please": {example}.
textarea.bp7: {medium} is a size alias of {default}. New code should use {small}, {default}, or {large}.
textarea.bp8: Always give the control an accessible name: a visible label or {ariaLabel}.

theme-switcher.title: Theme Switcher
theme-switcher.description: Light, System, and Dark in one control. It reads and writes the shared geist-theme store.
theme-switcher.callout: The live control below changes the docs theme. {forcedTheme} is a locked preview and does not write storage.
theme-switcher.defaultHint: Three labeled options. The thumb tracks the current theme from useTheme.
theme-switcher.smallHint: Pass {small} for footers and menus. Keep the default size on a settings page.
theme-switcher.disabledHint: {disabled} is for a read-only preview of the control. Prefer {forcedTheme} when the app itself locks the palette.
theme-switcher.forcedThemeHint: {forcedTheme} locks the thumb on light or dark and disables the group. Use it when the surrounding surface cannot follow System.
theme-switcher.useThemeHint: Call {setTheme} from settings or a menu. Do not mirror the value into a second local ref.
theme-switcher.useThemeBody: {initTheme} runs once on the client, reads {localStorage} key {storageKey}, and toggles {darkClass} on {documentElement}. {system} follows {prefersColorScheme}.
theme-switcher.practice1: One Theme Switcher per app — footer or settings. Do not drop a second copy on every page.
theme-switcher.practice2: Use this control for Light / System / Dark. Do not rebuild it with {switch} or three icon buttons.
theme-switcher.practice3: {small} for dense chrome. Default size when the labels have room to breathe.
theme-switcher.practice4: Read and write through {useTheme}. Mirroring the value into local page state will desync the thumb.
theme-switcher.practice5: {forcedTheme} is the lock when a surface cannot follow System. {disabled} is only for a static preview of the control.
theme-switcher.practice6: Leave the Light / System / Dark labels alone. They already have per-option {ariaLabel}s.

toast.title: Toast
toast.description: Short, temporary acknowledgment of a user action. useToasts mounts a Toaster on the first call.
toast.defaultHint: message is the neutral type. Pass a string or an object with a text field.
toast.typesHint: Pick the method from how the user experienced the event, not from the HTTP status.
toast.previewHint: Toast renders one item. useToasts pushes into a shared list and mounts Toaster if the page has none.
toast.previewWarmPool: Warm pool restarted in IAD. Sticky sessions keep the same egress IP for the next 30 minutes.
toast.preserveHint: preserve skips the auto-dismiss timer. Use it only when the user must read or act before it disappears.
toast.previewCopyToken: Copy this token now. It will not be shown again.
toast.actionHint: action is the button label. onAction runs, then the toast dismisses. Action toasts stay up for 8 seconds.
toast.undoHint: onUndoAction paints a button labeled Undo. Only use it when rollback is safe.
toast.richTextHint: text can be a string or a VNode. Keep it to one short phrase — toasts are not a document.
toast.bestPractice1a: Non-blocking confirmations of something the user just did:
toast.bestPractice2: Field validation stays on the input. Persistent warnings stay in Note or Banner. Billing or build failures need a durable row plus a short toast.
toast.bestPractice3a: Pick the method from the user's experience. A canceled deploy is
toast.bestPractice4a: Default toasts auto-dismiss (4s, 6s for error, 8s with an action).
toast.bestPractice4b: only when the user must act.
toast.bestPractice5: One toast at the end of an async flow. Do not narrate every hop.
toast.bestPractice6a: Completion copy is a noun plus a past participle:
toast.bestPractice6b: . Never "successfully". Skip the period on a single sentence.
toast.bestPractice7a: Error toasts are two sentences with periods and a recovery step:
toast.bestPractice8a: Match the toast verb to the button: Delete Project then
toast.bestPractice9a: The undo label is the word
toast.bestPractice9b: . Only offer it when rollback is safe.
toast.bestPractice10: Do not put primary navigation in a toast. The surface disappears before keyboard users can reach it.

toggle.title: Toggle
toggle.description: Flip a single boolean. Not Switch — Switch is a 2–3 option segmented control.
toggle.defaultHint: v-model owns the boolean. checked / {'@change'} also work if the parent already stores the flag that way.
toggle.sizesHint: default is 16px track, medium is 20px, large is 24px.
toggle.colorHint: On-state track. blue is the default. amber and red are for caution and destructive policies.
toggle.label: Label
toggle.labelHint: Children are the visible name. direction flips the track to the leading edge. labelCasing stays title unless the copy is already sentence case.
toggle.practiceOnOff: Toggle is one immediate on/off. Lists of optional rows use Checkbox. Two or three mutually exclusive views use Switch.
toggle.practiceLabelBefore: Label the thing that is true when on:
toggle.practiceAccessibleBefore: Give an accessible name with children,
toggle.practiceAccessibleAfter: . Dev mode warns if all three are missing.
toggle.practiceDisable: Disable only when the flip is impossible (plan lock, policy). Say why next to the control or in a Tooltip.
toggle.practiceLabelCasingAfter: unless the surrounding sentence is already lowercase.

tooltip.title: Tooltip
tooltip.description: A short floating note on hover or focus. Explains a constraint, not the visible label.
tooltip.positionHint: Default is top. Compact API: pass text and wrap the trigger.
tooltip.noDelayHint: delay is on by default (~150ms). Set delay to false only for dense icon toolbars.
tooltip.boxAlignHint: boxAlign shifts the floating box along the side: left, center (default), right.
tooltip.customTextHint: Use the text slot when the note needs emphasis or a Kbd.
tooltip.tipAndAlignmentHint: tip hides the arrow. {'center={false}'} left-aligns longer copy.
tooltip.retentionHobby: Retention is 14 days on the Hobby plan.
tooltip.bestPractice1: Visible label names the control. Tooltip adds the limit, scope, or why it is disabled.
tooltip.bestPractice2: One sentence or fragment. Sentence case. No period on a single fragment.
tooltip.bestPractice3: Do not repeat the button text or say “Click to…”. Entity previews with rows of facts belong on Context Card.
tooltip.bestPractice4: Keep the default delay. Icon-only triggers still need their own {ariaLabel} — the tooltip does not replace it.
tooltip.bestPractice5: Do not wrap a labelled Input. Put help on a sibling icon button so the field keeps a single name.

typography.title: Typography
typography.description: Geologica everywhere, Geist Mono for code and tokens. Page letter-spacing is −2%.
typography.scaleHint: We do not ship text-heading-* utilities. Use these sizes so product and docs stay aligned.
typography.colorSecondary: Secondary lines, meta, icons at rest:
typography.colorInlineCode: Inline code stays Geist Mono at 13px, same color as surrounding text unless it is a token.
typography.practiceControls: Controls are 13px. Do not drop a 16px label next to an h-8 input.
typography.practiceTitleCase: Title Case button labels that name the action: Deploy Project, Add Email.
typography.practiceUppercase: Uppercase only for tiny meta (repo row, calendar caps), and pair it with 12px.
typography.practiceTabularNums: Tabular nums for usage, dates in tables, and gauge values.

video.title: Video
video.description: Embed a clip with lazy load, loop, and a compact control bar.
video.defaultHint: src is required. lazy, loop, and controls default to true. Pass width and height so the frame keeps ratio before metadata arrives.
video.noControlsHint: Without controls the clip is decorative: muted, autoplay, no chrome.
video.bestPractice1: Keep {lazy} on in product views so the file waits for the viewport. Docs previews set it false so the first paint is a frame, not a hole.
video.bestPractice2: Set {width} and {height} together. The wrapper uses them as an aspect-ratio lock.
video.bestPractice3: Use controls when the clip is the content. Drop them for ambient loops in a hero or empty state.
video.bestPractice4: Pass {poster} when the first frame is black or a flash. Do not restyle the built-in bar.
video.bestPractice5: This is not a player product. Long-form or chapters stay on the host page, not inside Video.
